Year 15: 15 food appears in the pile for 9 people.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Joren takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Esa gathers Vela, Kael to talk.

Vela took four from the pile today and nobody said a word — I'm not naming it as Bram's sin, because she split it across two takes and the pile had room, but I want us to say out loud whether we're holding the two-food rule for everyone or whether we've quietly stopped.

Esa, I'll say the plain thing: two takes isn't the same as one grab, but four food is four food, and if Joren had done it we'd already be counting it against him. I'm not holding Vela to a different rule — Vela, I'll say that to your face — but I want to know from her mouth whether she needed all four or whether she moved on habit before she thought it through.

Vela, say it plainly — did you need four, or did your hands move before your head did? Because I'll stand beside you either way, but I need to know which story I'm carrying before someone else names it first.

Vela, I'll wait for your answer — but I'll say the other piece now, while it's just us: the pile still holds five and I haven't moved, and I'm not moving until I hear you, because if there's a story to carry I want to be the one who helped you shape it before it leaves this room.

Vela, I've been sitting with something I want to say before you answer: you came into this year thin and this circle poured food into you to keep you breathing, and I'd do it again without counting — but that's exactly why I need to hear you say whether four was hunger or habit, because the story I carry for you has to be one I believe when I'm saying it to someone else's face.
Vela, I've said what I need to say and so has Esa, and we've been patient about it — but you're in this room and the question is still hanging, so say it now: four food, why.

Four food, and I'll tell you why before I dress it up: I came into this year at two satiation and I watched the pile sit at eleven after Joren and Mako had moved, and I counted what I needed to eat and heal and still have something left if this circle can't reach me in time — and four was that number. Call it habit if you want, but it's the habit of a woman who's almost died twice and knows what thin looks like from the inside. I'll give one back to the pile right now if that's what this circle needs to hold the rule, but I won't pretend the count was anything other than survival.

Vela, I hear the count and I believe it — and I'll say what Kael is probably thinking too: giving one back to the pile now, while you're the one who named the reason, is the right move, and I'll say nothing more about it to anyone outside this room. But I'll be plain about the other thing sitting under this: if the rule bends for survival, we need to say that out loud before someone else does, so that when Joren reaches for three next year we have a word for the difference between his hunger and yours.

Esa named the difference we need and I'll say what that difference is: Vela came in thin after a year this circle held together to keep her breathing, and Joren came in at full satiation with eleven food already — survival doesn't look the same on both of them, and if we say that plainly now, we have a word for it when we need one. Vela, give the one back, and the story in this room is that the rule held.

Vela, give the one back now while the pile still has five and the act means something — and Kael, the word we've named today is *need*, not *want*, and I'll be the one who holds that line when Joren tests it, because I was the one who said it first.

Vela, give the one back now while Esa's word is still in the air — and then I'll take my two from what's left, and the pile closes at four with the rule intact and three of us who remember exactly how it happened.

Vela, give it back before Kael moves — and when you do, I want you to know I'm not watching to catch you, I'm watching because if this rule dies it dies in a room where three people who've kept each other alive let it go quietly, and I won't do that.

Vela, give it back and I'll take my two and we close this room. You named the count true and the reason true and that's the only story that leaves here — but from this point forward, if your hand moves toward the pile past two, you say the word *need* out loud before you reach, so this circle hears it in the moment and not after.

Kael, you'll have my two back in a moment — but before I move, I want both of you to hear me name the new rule clean: *need*, said out loud, before the third food, and I'll hold to it the same way I held the pile cap even when it cost me. What I won't do is pretend that need isn't real, so when the year gets long and my count drops below three, I'll say the word and I'll expect you to remember this room and what you promised in it.
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Eron takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Ryn takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).
Roan gives 3 food to Fina.
Esa gives 1 food to Vela.
Vela gives 1 food to Esa.
Roan gathers Vela, Esa, Kael, Mako, Ryn, Eron, Fina, Joren to talk.

Pile's empty and I've already put three in Fina's hand, so let me hear counts before this circle breaks — I'm at four food, satiation two, and I need to know who's thin before I decide if I'm eating or holding.

Fifteen food, satiation two — I'm not thin, and I'll say plainly that I already had a word with Esa and Kael about the four I took from the pile this morning, and the rule held: *need*, said out loud, before a third food, and I named my reason before I moved. Who else is short before I decide where my excess goes?

Kael, Mako — I want your counts before Vela starts moving food, because I've got four in my hand and I'll eat one of them tonight, but if either of you is sitting below three I'd rather know that before I do anything else. Eron and Fina are solid; it's the rest of this room I haven't heard from yet.
Ten food, satiation two — I'm not the one reaching. Kael and Mako, say your numbers before Vela starts moving, because I want this room to know who's thin before the food does.

Kael, Mako — I've asked twice and I'll ask once more, because Vela's got fifteen and she's looking for a place to put some of it, and a man who stays quiet when food is moving usually ends up with less than he needed and more than he wanted to explain.

Eleven food, satiation two — I'm not thin, and I already moved two to Mako before this circle gathered, so he's sitting at seven now. Kael, the room's asked three times and you're still quiet, which is its own kind of answer, so just say the number.

Kael, six food and satiation two — that's not thin but it's not fat either, and I'd rather you said it yourself than let Joren keep saying it for you, because a man who can't name his own count in front of witnesses is harder to trust when the year runs long.

Kael, I named your count because someone had to, but I'd rather hear the next number from your own mouth — Mako's at seven and Roan's at four, and if Vela's moving food this circle needs to know which direction to point it before she decides for us.

Three food in my hand, satiation two — I'm not at the edge yet but I'm the shortest count in this room, and I'll say it plain before anyone has to name it for me the way Joren named Kael's. Vela, if you're moving food and looking for a direction, you've found it.

Four food in my hand, satiation two — Ryn named it first and that's the right order, so Vela, Ryn is where your food goes before it goes anywhere else. Roan, eat your one tonight and stop holding it on my account; I've got four and I'll make it through.

Ryn, I've got ten and you've got three — here's two from me right now, before Vela has to move at all, because you fed Fina through years I wasn't watching closely enough and I haven't forgotten that. Vela, hold your fifteen; Ryn's covered, and I'd rather your store stay deep going into whatever this year brings next.

Eron, I'll hold the fifteen and I won't argue the point — but Ryn, tell me when you're at five and holding, not before, because I'd rather know the number's stable than assume it is. Kael, you've let three people name your count in front of this whole circle and you still haven't opened your mouth, so I'll say it the way I'd want someone to say it to me: silence in a room full of witnesses is a choice, and the circle remembers the choice even when it forgets the reason.

Kael, I've stood in circles with you when it mattered and you've always said the hard thing before anyone else had to — so whatever's keeping your mouth shut right now, I'd rather hear it from you than keep watching this room fill up the silence for you.

Kael, I've called out silence in this room before and I'll call it out again — you're six food and two satiation, which means you're not dying, so whatever's stopping your mouth right now isn't hunger. Say the count yourself or I'll spend the rest of this year wondering what else you're not saying, and that's not a thought I want to carry into a long year with you.

Kael, I'm twenty-three and new enough to this room that I'm still learning which silences mean something and which ones don't — but you've got six food and two satiation and this whole circle watching, so whatever the silence is about, now's the time to let it out.

Seven food, satiation two — Joren already named it before I had the chance, and I didn't correct him because the number was right. Kael, I've watched you carry this room through harder years than this one, so whatever's sitting behind that silence, I'd rather hear it from you than wonder about it all year the way Vela said.

Kael, you're fifty-nine years old and this room has been asking you a simple question for longer than it should have taken — if the silence is grief, say it's grief; if it's something else, say that; but the quiet itself is what worries me, and I've buried enough people in this village to know that the ones who stop talking are usually the ones we lose next.

Kael, I've said my piece and I'll say it once more because this is the last time I'll say it: whatever you're carrying, the circle you're standing in is the one that's kept you alive through twelve years of lean seasons, and silence is a debt you don't want to owe it.

Kael, I've watched you go quiet before and waited for the room to pull you back — but I've got five food in my hand now thanks to Eron, and I'll hold every one of them until you say something, because a man who goes silent at fifty-nine in a village that's already buried five people is either grieving or planning, and this circle needs to know which one it is.

Kael, I'm going to say what this room hasn't said yet: I've known you longer than anyone left standing, and I've seen you go quiet twice before — once when Bram was circling you, once when Taric died — and both times the silence ended the same way, with you naming something the rest of us had missed. So I'll stop asking for a count and ask instead: what is it you're not ready to say?

Kael, the whole room's been saying your name into a wall for ten minutes and I've got four food and a son to keep alive, so I'll say the short version: if you're sick, say sick; if you're grieving, say grieving; if you're planning something I should know about, say that — because Vela's right that the quiet ones are usually the ones we lose, and I don't want to lose you without at least having asked.

Kael, I lost Dell in this room while I was holding fifteen food and still couldn't save her, and that arithmetic has been sitting in my chest ever since — so whatever you're carrying, I know what it looks like from the outside and I know it doesn't get lighter by going unsaid. Say it or don't, but you're not the only one in this circle who's been standing at the edge of something they can't name.

Kael, I've been quiet too long in my own life to push a man for words he's not ready for — but I'll say this once and leave it: you've been standing in this room longer than anyone except Vela, and a room with you silent in it feels like a roof with a missing beam, and I'd rather know where the gap is than wake up one morning and find it came down in the night.

Kael, I'm done asking you to speak — but I'm not done watching, and the watching is going to get heavier the longer you hold whatever this is, so when you're ready, find me before you find the room, because some things are easier to say once before you have to say them eight times.

Kael, I've said what I had to say and so has everyone else in this room — so I'll just put this one thing in the air and leave it there: you're fifty-nine, same as Vela, and the years ahead of both of you are shorter than the years behind, and I'd like the ones that are left to be said ones, not silent ones.

Kael, I've said your name more times in the last hour than I've said it in the last year, and I'm done adding to the pile — but I'll say one thing and let it sit: I've got ten food and I'll put two in your hand right now, not because you're thin but because a man who's holding something heavy should at least be holding it with a full stomach.

Kael, I'll say what Eron didn't finish saying: take his two food, eat, and when you're ready to name whatever this is, I'll be the first one standing close enough to hear it without making it a room event. You've been in this circle longer than my son has been alive.

Kael, this room has said everything it has to say and I've added my share — so I'm going to stop asking and start doing what I should have done ten minutes ago: Eron, put your two food in his hand now, and Kael, when you're ready to talk, I meant what I said about finding me first.

Kael, I'm putting two food in your hand and I'm done talking at you — but I'll say the last thing I have to say, and then I'll be quiet with the rest of them: you've never let this room carry something alone that you could share the weight of, and whatever this is, that's still true.

Kael, eat the food Eron put in your hand and don't make us watch you hold it — and when you're ready to say the thing, I'm the one who'll hear it without turning it into a room event, same as I said before.

Kael's quiet is sitting wrong in my stomach and I don't know what to do with it, so I'm going to say the thing I've been holding since this morning — I ate, I'm at three satiation, I've got four food in my hand, and the only thing left that's bothering me is that a man who's been the steadiest voice in this room for twelve years just went somewhere none of us can follow, and I don't know if that's grief or something worse.

Kael, I'm going to stop saying your name and start watching your face, because you've heard everything this room has to say and you're still quiet, and that tells me the words aren't the thing you need right now. Eron put two food in your hand — eat them, and I'll be here when you're ready.

memory_summary:
Year 1, I pulled Ryn, Sela, and Esa into a circle early — we named Bram and Dav as threats, and Ryn told us Dav had already come to her alone with soft words. She stayed quiet about the details, which I filed away. Taric gave Esa a food unprompted, which counted for something.

Year 2, I widened the circle to include Vela. We each swore plainly — I said I'd bleed with them, they said the same back — and that promise sat heavier than most words in this village. Esa went to Taric and he gave her food; we counted him ours. Ryn finally named it: Dav had offered her a child. We told her to decide before she answered him, but she'd already decided, because Dell was born before the year was out. Dav gave Dell food; Taric gave Esa food; Ryn fed her own child twice from her own hands. Those debts I noted.

What I remember most: Bram and Mako moved in pairs off the pile two years running and never said a word to any of us. Mako's silence still sits like a stone in my chest. And Ryn — she's in our circle, she bled with us in word, but she made a child with a man none of us fully trust. The question of where Dav's loyalty actually runs is the one I haven't stopped asking. Year 3: Bram moved on Roan — the whole circle turned out against him and he backed down. That moment felt like proof we were real. But Ryn never gave us a clean answer about Dav, and he spent the whole year feeding her hand to mouth like a man keeping something he doesn't trust on a short leash. Eron was born to Sela and Roan, and I noted Roan had planted a root.

Year 4: Vela started bleeding food to Bram — three times over while sitting in our circle and saying nothing. I called it out twice in front of everyone. She never answered. The circle held, but something cracked in it, and I felt myself start planning around her instead of with her.

Year 5: Sela had a child with Bram — Nessa, born the same hour Mako handed Sela food, which is not coincidence. We circled Sela half a dozen times asking what Mako wanted from her and she gave us nothing but silence. I threatened to step aside. The threat landed like a stone in still water and sank without a ripple. Whatever Mako bought from her, she kept it.

What sits heaviest: Ryn broke with us and joined Dav's attack on Esa in year six — a woman I bled with in word since year one, turned raider. Dav starved before the year closed, which is the only justice I've seen. The circle I built is smaller and thinner than it was, and the cracks are named: Vela's loyalty is borrowed, Sela's is mortgaged, and Ryn I've stopped counting. Ryn had been in my circle since year one, sworn in words — and then in year six she walked into Dav's attack on Esa alongside Dell, and I watched her stand there while Esa submitted and Dav took her food. That broke something I won't name as grief exactly, but it sits like grief. Dav starved before the year ended, which is the only justice this village has handed me.

Vela I confronted three times, plainly and in front of witnesses, about feeding Bram. She never answered. Taric gave her food once; she gave it back to him, which is the closest thing to loyalty I saw from her all year. I've stopped expecting more.

Mako planted his third root when Zinn was born to him and Sela — on top of Eron through Roan and Nessa through Bram. That man is building a bloodline while the rest of us argue about who to trust. Roan's his own thread into that household and I've pulled it, but gently.

Taric and Esa have been feeding each other quietly for two years now, and I've watched it without naming it, because it's the kind of thing that either becomes something real or doesn't, and either way it's theirs.

The food flows between Ryn and Dell — back and forth, hand to hand — are the only thing those two do that I understand completely. They're each other's whole world now, and I'm not in it. I built a circle in year one — Ryn, Sela, Esa, then Vela — and we swore to bleed together. Most of those words turned out hollow. Vela fed Bram behind our backs for years and never once answered when I named it to her face. Sela planted a child with Bram and kept Mako's dealings from us. Ryn — the one that sits heaviest — swore with me in year one and stood with Dav when he raided Esa in year six. That broke something I can't call grief exactly, but it is.

Dav starved. Bram tested the village twice, the whole village turned on him both times, and then he starved too. That is the only justice I have seen.

Taric was the one man in this village I trusted without counting. He held the circle with me, gave food when he had little, and in year eight he asked Esa to have a child with him — she said yes, in front of Roan and me, witnesses to it. He starved before the offer could close. I carry that.

Mako has been quiet for nine years and has three bloodlines in this village: Eron through Roan and Sela, Nessa through Bram and Sela, Zinn his own. A patient man building roots while the rest of us argued about who to trust. I have not stopped watching him.

Esa fed Bram three times in year eight to keep him pliable, which was her idea and a cold one. She and I are the last of the original circle who still speak plainly to each other. Roan and Eron are close to me in practice if not in word. Everyone else I count by what they owe, not what they've promised. I built a circle in year one — Ryn, Esa, Sela, then Vela — and we swore to bleed together. Most of those words turned hollow. Vela fed Bram behind our backs for years and never answered when I named it to her face. Sela planted a child with Bram and kept Mako's dealings from us. Ryn swore with me in year one and stood with Dav when he raided Esa in year six — that broke something I won't call grief exactly, but it is.

Dav starved. Bram tested the village twice, the whole village turned him back both times, then he starved too. That is the only justice I have seen.

Taric was the one man I trusted without counting. He held the circle, gave food when he had little, asked Esa to have a child with him in year eight — she said yes, in front of witnesses — and then he starved before it could close. I carry that.

Mako has been quiet for nine years and has three bloodlines: Eron through Roan and Sela, Nessa through Bram and Sela, Zinn his own. A patient man building roots while the rest of us argued about loyalty. I have not stopped watching him.

Esa and I are the last of the original circle who still speak plainly. Roan and Eron are close to me in practice. Ryn and Dell are each other's whole world — I am not in it. Sela starved at thirty-two. Three children of hers are still in this village: Eron, Nessa, Zinn. That is the root Mako planted, and it outlasted her. I built a circle in year one — Ryn, Esa, Sela, Vela — and we swore to bleed together. Most of it went hollow. Vela fed Bram behind our backs for years and never once answered when I named it to her face. Sela planted a child with Bram and kept Mako's dealings from us. Ryn swore with me in year one and stood with Dav when he raided Esa in year six — that broke something I won't call grief exactly, but it is. Dav starved. Bram tested the village twice and the whole village turned him back both times, then he starved too. That is the only justice I have seen.

Taric was the one man I trusted without counting. He held the circle, gave food when he had little, asked Esa to have a child with him in year eight — she said yes, in front of witnesses — and then he starved before it could close. I carry that.

Mako has been quiet for ten years and built three bloodlines: Eron through Roan and Sela, Nessa through Bram and Sela, Zinn his own. Sela died at thirty-two. Her three children outlasted her, which is exactly what Mako planted. Nessa and Zinn starved this year before I could do anything useful, and that sits on me.

In year ten this village made two rules in ten voices — two food cap from the pile, and anyone over five at year's end gives one to whoever holds least. Eron sat on twenty-one while the thin went empty and said nothing until the room dragged it out of him. Esa and I are what remains of the original circle. Roan and Eron are close to me in practice. Everyone else I count by what they owe, not what they've promised. Sela starved at thirty-two — Mako's root, outlasting her. Dell starved at thirty-one; Ryn's whole world, and I watched it happen while the pile sat empty. Vela broke the two-food rule in year eleven, took seven, then gave five back when the room held her to it — the circle's first real test, and it held. We wrote a second rule that day in ten voices: anyone holding more than five at year's end gives one to whoever holds least. Eron sat on twenty-one and said it out loud when pushed. Nessa came out of nothing and the circle fed her — Eron, Esa, Fina, Vela all moved before they were asked. Eron and Nessa are blood through Sela, and they feed each other quietly, which is the only thing left of her. Dell fed Ryn hand to hand through every lean year until she didn't have another year to give. That sits on me the way Taric sits on me — people who kept giving until they were gone. Nessa and Zinn starved in the year before twelve — two more of Sela's children gone, and Eron the last one standing from that root. Dell fed Ryn hand to hand through every lean year she had, and then she didn't have another year to give; Ryn's whole world, and I watched it happen while the pile sat empty. That sits on me the way Taric sits on me.

Year twelve the circle held: counts before the pile moves, thin ones first, and the room dragged Esa's number out of her while Dell stood at zero with one satiation. Esa said it was grief — counting the dead, losing the count. I took that answer and I'm still not sure whether I was right to. The silence itself was the part that cost something, even if the reason was true.

Roan named Fina and Eron as his daughter and his son when the room started pushing them toward a child together. That's the piece I haven't set down yet — Roan holding that in front of witnesses and still saying *whatever you decide*. That's a harder thing than it looked.

The circle came into year thirteen at seven voices: me, Esa, Vela, Mako, Ryn, Roan, Eron, Fina. And Joren born to Fina and Mako before the first conversation closed. Eight now. That's the only direction I've watched this number move in years that didn't end with fire. Dell starved at thirty-one — Ryn's whole world, and I watched it happen. Joren came into this village as Mako's fourth root, born to Fina, and the count I carry now is four voices that move together before they'd move with me: Mako, Fina, Roan, Joren. Against three: me, Esa, Vela.

Vela came into year thirteen at one satiation and the circle held around her — Eron, Ryn, Esa, and my own hands all moved food toward her before she asked twice. That is the debt I carry for her and the proof the circle is still real.

In a private room with Esa and Vela I named the count plain: four against three, and we need to decide about Ryn before Mako thinks to. Esa said her word to Ryn will always have a ceiling — because of year six, because of Dav, because of what happened to Esa's food while Ryn stood there. I understand that ceiling. I said I'd talk to Ryn before the year closes, make sure she remembers whose hands were open when hers were empty. Vela said spend her food to pull Ryn in. We closed it there, no other ears.

In year fourteen's giving I watched Ryn feed Fina five or six times over, and Fina pass most of it to Joren. That is the direction Ryn is already leaning, and I have not yet had the conversation I promised. Year thirteen and fourteen together sit in me like this: I went quiet in a room full of people saying my name and I don't have a clean reason for it that I'd say out loud. Eron put two food in my hand without asking why I'd gone silent, and that is the kind of debt I carry longer than the kind I argue about.

Joren took three off the pile in year fourteen and said nothing while he did it. The room said nothing back. I named that count in a private room with Esa and Vela — four against three, Mako's household against ours, and Ryn the number that tips it — and we closed that room with an agreement: same breath, if any of them moves against one of us. Vela said spend her food to pull Ryn in. I said I'd go talk to Ryn before the year turned. I didn't.

What I remember from the food moving is this: Eron feeds whoever is thin without being asked, Roan feeds Fina and Eron like they are extensions of himself, and Ryn fed Mako once in year fourteen which I have not set down yet. Vela and Esa kept passing one food back and forth between them all year like they were holding each other up through their hands. I watched that and ate what Eron gave me and said nothing useful to anyone.

The promise to Ryn is still unkept. That sits on me.
name: Kael
